plan: Mechanism is equivalent to a second-price auction: highest sealed bid wins and pays the second-highest bid. With independent private values and risk neutrality, bidding one’s true value is a weakly dominant strategy. Overbidding risks negative profit by winning above value; underbidding risks losing profitable cases when the price would be below value. Therefore, I will set my exit price equal to my value ($30). If there’s a tie at 30, the winner is randomized; expected profit remains optimal.

[ This mechanism is effectively a second-price auction: highest sealed bid wins and pays the second-highest bid (the price when the penultimate bidder exits). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit and avoids the risks of overbidding (possible negative payoff) or underbidding (unnecessarily losing when profitable). With value 28 and no informative history (only 1 round), bid exactly 28 to maximize expected profit. ]

[ This is strategically equivalent to a second-price (Vickrey) auction: the highest sealed bid wins and pays the second-highest. The weakly dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding my value guarantees I only win when profitable (price ≤ value) and maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. There is only 1 round, so no learning or reputation effects. Therefore, set my sealed bid equal to my private value of $22 to ensure rational exit in the ascending clock and optimal payoff. ]
